output.brief:
Don't roll back the gateway. The regression comes from the storage compaction tuning change pushed on the evening of 2 Nov, not from gateway 5.8. In every cell that received that push, disk use jumped from about 41% to 97% within five minutes. Disk read waits rose from 9 ms to 205 ms, and p99 rose within minutes of each push. This happened regardless of when 5.8 arrived in the cell. One cell, aps-3, has 5.8 but skipped the push, and its p99 stayed at about 94 ms. A test rollback of euw-1 to 5.7 changed nothing. A rollback would also reopen the security hole that must be closed by 30 Nov. Network and traffic growth don't explain it: round-trip times are normal, and GET traffic is up only 6%.

Next step: revert the compaction change in one cell and watch GET p99 and backlog. If p99 recovers, extend the revert to the other cells. Backlog was 11.2% before the push against a 15% danger point. Watch it closely and consider a modest compaction increase or a rate limit on Orrin if needed. Wait for the 10 Nov attribution before pacing Orrin. Don't pause compaction. I'm fairly confident (about 90%) in the main diagnosis. What drove the backlog growth is still unattributed.
